title: Major Bank Levy
summary: From 1 July 2017 banks with liabilities over $100 billion pay a levy of 0.06% a year on certain liabilities.

commenced.what: Levy applies to quarters from 1 July 2017

direction_rationale: The levy raises the five largest banks' funding costs relative to smaller banks, which may help challengers or be passed on to all borrowers.
comparison: Banks above versus below $100 billion in liabilities

assessment.summary: A levy of 0.06% a year on the liabilities of the five largest banks. It narrows their funding cost advantage over smaller banks, but as a tax on one set of firms' funding it can be passed on to borrowers.

marks.reason: A tax on some banks' liabilities distorts funding costs and can be passed on to all borrowers.
Narrows the major banks' funding cost advantage over smaller rivals.
